## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- AI can now track body movements through walls using WiFi-DensePose technology.
- ChatGPT introduces interactive visuals for math explanations.
- NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3 Super, a 120B open model for agents.
- ElevenLabs launches ElevenCreative, a full creative platform for generating, editing, and localizing audio and video.
- Perplexity merges its agent with a Mac mini for continuous operation.
- Anthropic opens a research institute to study AI's impact on jobs, economies, law, and governance.

### Detailed Points
- WiFi-DensePose picks up shifts in WiFi signal reflections to reconstruct full body positions in real-time, allowing for tracking through walls.
- ChatGPT's interactive visuals enable users to adjust variables and watch formulas change in real-time, making math explanations more engaging.
- NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Super delivers 5× higher throughput than the previous model, with a 1M-token context window.
- ElevenCreative combines voice cloning, text-to-speech, AI video, music, sound effects, and image generation with a browser-based editor and 70+ language support.
- Perplexity's merge with Mac mini enables continuous operation, working across local files, apps, and sessions 24/7.
- Anthropic's research institute will study how AI reshapes various aspects of society, with direct access to frontier model data.
- Other tools and developments mentioned include BrainGrid, SureThing, AnveVoice, Aivyx, TriviaPixel, Veemo AI, Remodeler IQ, LLMfit, Context Hub, and NotebookLM-py.

newsletters.subject: 🔥 Google Gemini Embedding 2: multimodal search across 5 media types
newsletters.summary:
## AlphaSignal

### Key Highlights
- Google releases Gemini Embedding 2, a multimodal embedding model that maps text, images, video, audio, and PDFs together, allowing for retrieval across different media types.
- Anthropic introduces /btw, a feature that enables users to ask contextual questions without interrupting Claude Code tasks.
- Hume AI presents TADA, an open-source speech model that reduces hallucinations and generates speech 5× faster.
- Lambda releases benchmark results for open-weight models, allowing for comparisons of model performance.
- OpenAI rolls out interactive math and science explanations in ChatGPT.

### Detailed Points
- **Google Gemini Embedding 2**: This model uses representation learning to store information across nested vector dimensions, with default embeddings using 3,072 dimensions for full semantic representation. It supports interleaved multimodal input and can process text inputs up to 8,192 tokens, up to six images per request, video clips up to 120 seconds, raw audio directly into embeddings, and PDF documents up to six pages.
- **Anthropic /btw**: This feature allows users to ask contextual questions without interrupting Claude Code tasks, enabling more efficient and effective use of the platform.
- **Hume AI TADA**: TADA is an open-source speech-language model that generates text and speech in one synchronized stream, reducing common issues in LLM-based text-to-speech systems such as skipped words, hallucinated content, and slow inference. It aligns each text token with a single acoustic representation and has a real-time factor of 0.09, making it roughly 5× faster than comparable LLM-based TTS systems.
- **Lambda Benchmark Results**: Lambda's benchmark results provide a comparison of open-weight model performance, including model overview and specifications, sustained tok/s and P99 latency on NVIDIA A100, NVIDIA H100, and NVIDIA B200 GPUs, and side-by-side comparisons for vLLM and SGLang.
- **OpenAI Interactive Explanations**: OpenAI has added interactive visual modules to ChatGPT, enabling real-time exploration of math and science formulas and making learning more engaging and effective.
- **Other Updates**:
  - Google upgrades Workspace with Gemini tools that build spreadsheets, design slides, and summarize Drive content.
  - Embedl enables multimodal reasoning on edge devices with under 8GB RAM.
  - Anthropic creates a research institute focused on AI economics, governance, and risks.
  - Amazon launches a Health AI agent on its website and app for personalized health guidance and care access.

## World of AI Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- NVIDIA has released Nemotron 3 Super, a 120 billion parameter open-source reasoning model for agentic AI workloads, beating closed frontier models on benchmarks.
- Anthropic has updated Claude to work seamlessly across Excel and PowerPoint, allowing for continuous AI sessions without losing context.
- The AI economy is growing, and entrepreneurs are finding ways to monetize AI tools.

### Detailed Points
- NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Super model:
  - Built on a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts architecture.
  - Offers 4x memory efficiency over traditional models.
  - Has a 1 million token native context window.
  - Allows developers to control the reasoning budget for latency-sensitive applications.
  - Is open-source, with training datasets, reinforcement learning environments, and post-training recipes available.
- Anthropic's Claude update:
  - Enables full context sharing across Excel and PowerPoint.
  - Introduces "Skills" for reusable one-click workflows.
  - Supports Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry deployments.
- The AI industry is moving towards open-source models, with NVIDIA's release being a significant contender.
- Anthropic's update focuses on enterprise use cases, particularly in spreadsheet and slide deck applications.
- The pace of AI development is relentless, with companies like NVIDIA and Anthropic driving innovation.

## Uncovering AI

### Key Highlights
- Google has upgraded its viral image model to Nano Banana 2, which offers improved photorealism and character consistency.
- The new model can handle complex compositions with up to 14 distinct objects in a single scene and has achieved a significant breakthrough in character consistency.
- AI-generated content is becoming increasingly advanced, with potential applications in graphic novels, serialized social media content, and more.

## The Rundown AI

### Key Highlights
- Perplexity debuted Personal Computer, a new local version of its Computer AI agent system that runs on a dedicated Mac mini, positioning itself as a more secure, controlled rival to OpenClaw.
- Elon Musk announced the revival of Macrohard as a joint xAI-Tesla project, claiming the system can "emulate the function of entire companies."
- Google Workspace Studio allows users to create agentic workflows, reading form submissions, tracking them in a spreadsheet, and emailing action items.

### Detailed Points
- Perplexity's Personal Computer is an always-on local agent that can be managed from anywhere, offering safeguards like tracked activity and a "kill switch" to shut the system down.
- The system uses a Mac mini, unintentionally making it the default hardware for the AI agent era.
- Macrohard, now a joint xAI-Tesla project, aims to create a system that can emulate entire companies, using Grok with a Digital Optimus agent and Nvidia's AI4 chip.
- Musk's announcement came after reports of 20+ Macrohard engineer exits and a paused 600-person data project.
- Google Workspace Studio offers a step-by-step guide on creating an agent that reads form submissions, tracks them in a spreadsheet, and emails action items.

### AI Training
- Create agentic workflows in Google Workspace using Workspace Studio, which allows users to automate tasks and create customized workflows.
- The process involves setting up a flow, selecting a starter, and adding steps to read form submissions, track data, and email action items.

### Anthropic Institute
- Anthropic launched the Anthropic Institute, a new group combining three teams to study AI's societal impacts and document its disruption.
- The institute plans to share learnings from building frontier models with the public and engage workers and industries facing AI displacement.

### Community
- The Rundown AI features a community section, showcasing how readers use AI to work smarter, save time, or make life easier.
- Reader Jigar P. shared how he uses AI to support his son's communication and language development, generating tailored exercises and designing vocal and speech exercises.

## TLDR Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone will feature an iPad-like interface when opened, allowing for apps to run side-by-side for the first time.
- Elon Musk has unveiled a joint project between Tesla and xAI called 'Macrohard' aimed at creating a system capable of emulating the functions of software companies.
- Nvidia is reportedly planning its own open-source OpenClaw competitor.
- Meta is preparing to deploy four new homegrown chips to handle AI.

### Detailed Points
- The foldable iPhone's interior display will be roughly the size of an iPad mini, and the external screen will be about the size of a small iPhone's display. Apple is developing new iOS app layouts to adapt to the new interface.
- The 'Macrohard' project pairs xAI's Grok with a Tesla-developed AI agent that processes real-time computer screen video and keyboard and mouse actions. The system will run on Tesla's in-house AI4 chip paired with xAI's Nvidia-based server hardware.
- Anduril, an autonomous weapons maker, has doubled the size of its space unit by acquiring ExoAnalytic Solutions, a space intelligence firm.
- WordPress has launched a site that allows users to launch a web server, database, and full WordPress installation within a browser in about 30 seconds.
- Temporal, a JavaScript object, enables date and time management in various scenarios, such as time zone and calendar representation, wall-clock time conversions, arithmetics, and formatting.
- Wispr Flow, a voice layer used by 100,000+ developers, has launched on Android and allows users to speak naturally into their IDE, Claude Code, or ChatGPT.
- TLDR has announced a referral program, allowing users to get free swag by sharing their referral link with friends.
- The newsletter also covers various topics such as the journey to fix time in JavaScript, designing antibodies using AI, and the concept of institutional intelligence.

newsletters.summary:
## JournalClub.io

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from Hainan University, China, have developed a model called PassGLM that can guess passwords using personally identifiable information (PII) and old passwords.
- The model was trained on 8 databases of breached passwords and was able to crack nearly a third of target accounts within 100 guesses.
- The study highlights the importance of using random and unique passwords, as common password strategies are well-documented and can be exploited by attackers.
- The PassGLM model uses a combination of PII and password reuse patterns to guess passwords, outperforming existing approaches that rely solely on PII or password reuse.

### Detailed Points
- The study analyzed password creation behaviors and found that people often use common/popular passwords, reuse passwords, and embed personal information directly into passwords.
- The researchers used a probabilistic context-free grammar framework (PCFG) and a password reuse model called Pass2Path to develop the PassGLM model.
- The PassGLM model uses a fine-tuned language model to absorb complex human patterns and learn interactions between PII and password reuse.
- The model was evaluated in a simulation where the attacker is limited to a fixed number of guesses per account, and it was able to compromise roughly a third of accounts within 100 guesses.
- The study demonstrates that large language models (LLMs) can function as conditional probability estimators, not just text generators, and can learn complex patterns from structured behavioral data.
- The authors propose that incorporating old passwords into password guessing models can improve their effectiveness, as it allows the model to learn the joint distribution of PII and password reuse patterns.

newsletters.summary:
## Superhuman

### Key Highlights
- Perplexity launches Personal Computer, an always-on AI agent worker that lives on its own computer and does tasks for you.
- Anthropic upgrades Claude for Excel and PowerPoint with cross-app context and one-click skills.
- Amazon launches Health AI, a healthcare assistant available on its website and app.
- A study by ActivTrak finds that AI is intensifying work, not lightening it, and there's an optimal usage for AI, with employees who use AI tools 7-10% of their work hours having a productivity rate of 95%.

### Detailed Points
- Perplexity's Personal Computer is a persistent AI agent that runs on a continuously running Mac mini, giving its Comet Assistant 24/7 access to your files, apps, and sessions.
- Personal Computer operates in a secure local environment while remaining controllable from any device, anywhere, and functions as a "persistent digital proxy of you."
- Anthropic's Claude for Excel and PowerPoint now share full conversational context across all open files, allowing for continuous workflow without losing context.
- Amazon's Health AI can answer health questions, explain lab results, interpret medical records, manage prescription renewals, and book appointments, with the option to connect directly to a One Medical provider for over 30 common conditions.
- The study by ActivTrak found that employees who use AI tools see spikes in email time, business management tool usage, and weekend productivity, but AI-fueled productivity also hits a limit.
- The optimal usage for AI is 7-10% of work hours, with only 3% of users landing in this sweet spot.
- Other updates include Figma integrating directly into Anything, allowing for easy conversion of designs into code, and Replit launching Agent 4, the first AI built for creative collaboration between humans and agents.

## TLDR AI

### Key Highlights
- Replit launched Agent 4, introducing an infinite design canvas and the ability to run parallel AI agents to build backends and frontends simultaneously.
- Cursor is in talks with investors for a funding round that would value it at $50 billion, nearly double its valuation last fall.
- Meta has announced four new chips as part of an effort to diversify its hardware sources, reduce reliance on outside chipmakers, and bring down costs.

### Detailed Points
- Replit's Agent 4 update shifts from pure code generation to a collaborative product suite capable of shipping web apps, databases, and slide decks within a single integrated environment.
- Thoughtworks and Martin Fowler gathered a small group of technologists to discuss the future of software development with AI-native systems, raising questions about where engineering discipline goes when AI handles the code.
- The discussion centered around the "middle loop" of supervisory engineering, directing AI agents, and evaluating their output, as well as the decoupling of productivity and developer experience.
- Researchers from Google showed that enabling reasoning in large language models improved single-hop factual recall by acting as a computational buffer and generating related facts.
- NVIDIA released Nemotron 3 Super, a 120B open hybrid MoE model designed for agentic and multi-agent AI systems.
- Anthropic launched the Anthropic Institute to tackle AI's societal challenges, with key hires including Matt Botvinick, Anton Korinek, and Zoë Hitzig.
- Intrinsic, Open Robotics, Google DeepMind, and NVIDIA are running a global competition for developers and roboticists to train an AI model to handle dexterous cable insertion in simulation.
- Temporal's practical conference, Replay, will feature hands-on workshops for building real AI systems, with a discount available using the code TLDR75.
- NVIDIA is set to invest $2 billion in Nebius to expand AI cloud infrastructure.

newsletters.summary:
## The Code Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Perplexity has launched "Personal Computer", an always-on AI system that connects local files and apps to their cloud, powered by a dedicated Mac mini on their secure servers.
- The AI system acts as a digital proxy, managing tools and tasks from any device.
- Perplexity has also launched four new APIs: Search, Agent, Sandbox, and Embeddings, built on the same infrastructure and available for external use.
- Replit has shipped "Agent 4", a coding agent that enables teams to design on an infinite canvas while parallel agents handle front-end, back-end, and database work simultaneously.
- Google has launched "Gemini Embedding 2", its first natively multimodal embedding model, which maps text, images, video, audio, and documents into a single embedding space.

### Detailed Points
- Perplexity's Personal Computer is a significant development in AI technology, allowing for seamless integration of local files and apps with their cloud services.
- The launch of new APIs by Perplexity provides developers with more tools to build and integrate AI-powered applications.
- Replit's Agent 4 enables teams to work more efficiently, handling multiple tasks simultaneously and streamlining the development process.
- Google's Gemini Embedding 2 has the potential to revolutionize the way AI models process and understand different types of data, removing the need for separate pipelines.
- ElevenLabs' summit featured a discussion on the future of GenAI, with a focus on voice-driven interfaces and their potential to drive the next generation of AI technology.
- The newsletter also covers topics such as "AI brain fry", a cognitive tax that builds up from overseeing agents all day long, and the importance of documenting AI integration to avoid draining engineering resources.
- Notion has opened up a new engineering role, and there are various resources available for learning Claude Code, including tutorials and guides.
- The newsletter mentions a 16-part series to master DSA and build systems, as well as a dev who shipped an entire code with 5 autonomous agents.

## The Tech Buzz

### Key Highlights
- Real Intent is launching Superagent, a full-service growth automation platform for real estate agents and brokerages, at NAR '25.
- A live webinar is scheduled for March 12th at 1PM PST to introduce Superagent and demonstrate how it can help agents identify motivated sellers and buyers.
- Real Intent's solution is up to 90% more affordable than Zillow's Premier Agent service.
- Agents are seeing significant results, including increased seller meetings and listings, using Real Intent's platform.

### Detailed Points
- Real Intent's Superagent platform uses intent data to identify motivated sellers and buyers, providing agents with a competitive edge in their market.
- The platform is designed to automate tasks such as generating awareness, conversing with leads, and handing them off to agents.
- Real Intent is currently only working with one broker or agent per zip code, making it an exclusive opportunity for those who sign up.
- Agents who have used the platform have seen significant results, including:
  * One agent increased seller meetings by 2-fold and listed 2 properties in the first month.
  * An agent in the Southeast got a listing in their free trial week.
  * An agent in California asked to secure 2 more zip codes after a couple of weeks due to success.
  * A brokerage has secured an entire county.
- The live webinar will cover how intent data helps identify motivated sellers and buyers, the benefits of using Real Intent's solution, and real-world examples of agents successfully leveraging the platform.
- The webinar is expected to last around 30 minutes and will provide an opportunity for agents to learn about an effective and affordable alternative to Zillow's Premier Agent service.

## Mindstream

### Key Highlights
- Anthropic has launched a new institute, The Anthropic Institute, to study the biggest societal questions linked to advanced AI.
- The company says the institute will bring together research from across Anthropic and share insights that could help researchers, policymakers, and the public prepare for more powerful AI systems.
- Anthropic had a military contract with the Pentagon, but the contract was terminated after Anthropic asked about the usage of their models, and the Pentagon responded by blacklisting them from DoD-connected business.

### Detailed Points
- The Anthropic Institute will focus on studying the impact of advanced AI on society, including jobs, the economy, law, governance, and the values built into these systems.
- The institute will be led by Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark, who is also taking on the new role of Head of Public Benefit.
- Anthropic has announced a few early hires, including Matt Botvinick, who will lead work on AI and the rule of law, Anton Korinek, who will study how advanced AI could reshape economic activity, and Zoë Hitzig, who will link economics research to model training and development.
- The company is also expanding its Public Policy team, which will be led by Sarah Heck, Anthropic’s Head of External Affairs.
- Anthropic will open its first office in Washington, DC this spring as it grows its policy presence.
- The Pentagon situation seems to have accelerated Anthropic's growth rather than damaged it, with people seeing Anthropic hold its lines and deciding that was a company they trusted with their data.
- Anthropic launched a one-click migration tool letting you bring your full ChatGPT memory and conversation history straight into Claude, resulting in a 295% surge in ChatGPT uninstalls.
- Apple Music is partnering with TikTok to launch Play Full Song and Listening Party, two features that let Apple Music subscribers listen to full tracks directly inside TikTok.
